# Chapter Eighteen: Midnight Mass

Nero stood upon the stoop outside the large building, his eyes closed and heard pointed towards the heat of the sun he listened as the sounds of hammers and saws sung in the morning sky. People walked back and forth with a purpose as freshly cut wood entered the keep fixing the walls and ceiling. “Messenger Nero” called a voice, breaking Nero from his morning prayer. He smiled gently turning to regard the man, sweat on his brow and a smile on his face “Gildread, how goes the repairs” he asked amicably as his friend stepped forward up onto the steps of the old meeting hall. “Good Messenger, Meric doesn’t like my hours, but that’s just him” he began smiling down towards the rows of tents, knowing his partner was there somewhere ensuring things ran smoothly Nero followed his gaze and smiled knowingly “Have you decided a date yet?” he asked and watched Gilread turn bright red “Not yet messenger” he said and then quickly changed the subject “I just wanted to check on you, I know it’s been a few days, but you have seemed awfully quiet, are you okay?” Gilread asked gently putting his hand on the other man’s shoulder.

He had heard the whispers, known people had been talking since the other night, he had killed with his own hands, but what he had killed hadn’t been human it was a demon, a spawn created by Mages to assist in there subjugation of the entire country he thought bitterly. “Messenger, people are talking, they say you saved them, that you used the power of Aurtus to fend off the demons” Gilread whispered looking around to ensure they were alone. Nero smiled “I did no such thing Gilread, I simply defended myself and they went away after seeing one of their own killed, that is all” he answered. He felt uncomfortable with people attributing divine providence to him or his actions. Nero turned and walked into the old hall, looking up as he surveyed the progress of the repairs and nodded with appreciation. Things were going well here; the creatures had not returned, and the group had been left alone. They had received only one messenger from the Wardens stating that the army was on the move and then noting. Nero was worried about the outcome of that battle, but he wouldn’t show it on his face, he did not want people to start panicing.

The workers turned upon seeing him and shouted good natured hello’s waiving at the Messenger. Nero waved back smiling, it was good to have a flock he reflected, to have people to care for, to protect. “Messenger?” a female voice called, and he turned to find Vira, covered in dirt as she paused eyeing a main support “Hey, secure that support before you start adding planks across it guys” she yelled and the men waived down. Vira had taken over as foreman and had an amazing job Nero thought nodding to the woman.

“Have you eaten yet Messenger” she asked arching an eyebrow, He shot her a guilty look “No Vira, I was just about to” he confessed, and she motioned for him to join her. “Come on, I was just about to get something to eat. The two walked out of the large building and turned heading towards the tents where a line spread out across the yard. They joined the line and waited there turn.

“How are you feeling?” Vira asked shooting a concerned look at the Messenger. Nero shook his head, everyone seemed to have the same question for him since the incident a few days ago “I am fine Vira, honestly” he said giving the same answer he had the hundred times someone had asked him that question. “Repairs are going well it seems” he stated trying to change the subject, Vira gave him a look that said she knew exactly what he was doing but allowed him to steer the conversation. As they stood talking a commotion began at the front gate, Nero turned to look as a legion of soldiers began to flow in through the newly repaired gate, he studied them for a moment, fear rising in his soul but then was quickly replaced with relief as he saw the stylized eye and crown of Aurtus. “They came” he breathed, walking towards the gate and the soldiers.

As Nero approached the soldiers two men in familiar burgundy Messenger robes emerged from the group of soldiers, stepping out front and walking to intercept Nero. He knew those robes but had never thought to see them, not here and definitely not now. These were Emissaries for the Lord Regents he thought slowing his pace, the right hands of the Lord Regents for the two neighboring countries, it was obvious that what was going on in Vicor had everyone concerned enough that they thought Nero would need more then just a couple of protective guards.

Stepping up to the two Emissaries he bowed low greeting them “Good day Emissaries, I must say I am surprised to see you two here, how is it the Lord Regents for Lusor and Dever regard this enough of a priority to send their eyes and will to my humble country” he said. The taller of the two, a gaunt man who was advanced in age, the lines on his face telling a story of hardships early in life and his white hair though full lent to the look of age. “I am Emissary Loprin of Lusor, this is Emissary Hutchin of Dever, we have been sent to offer what assistance we can Lord Regent” he stated, presenting two sealed letters one from each of the countries Lord Regents, Nero took them returning the bow as a small glimmer of hope sparked in his belly “Please, our accommodations are spartan, but we will get you setup and rested, this evening we will sit down and talk more” he said motioning for the men to join him. Emissary Loprin paused, turning back to the crowd of soldiers “There is one more thing” he said and motioned with his hand as eight battered and worn Messengers appeared coming out of the soldiers to stand in front of Nero.

The newly minted Lord Regent of Vicor stepped forward as tears welled up in his eyes, he knew some of these men, these Messengers he thought lost “Welcome all, I know you have had a trying time and we will ensure you are well taken care of” he said and then turned to Loprin “How is it they come to be here?” he asked unbelievingly and the Emissary smiled. “We found them on the road, they were making their way North when we can upon them” he began and then the smile faded “Not all made it, Im sorry” he said and one of the Messengers stepped from the group, a small portly man with a shaved head, the deep lines on his face told of a man who smiled often. “Nero is it really you?” came the soft-spoken voice from the man and Nero turned his eyes widening “Horace Mcourt, by Aurtus, you are alive” he said rushing and embracing his friend and fellow Messenger.

“We escaped, after our people were massacred or taken, we escaped Nero, we failed them, failed all of them” Nero could see the distant look in his eyes, the man was in shock and Nero put an arm over his shoulder comforting him. “Its okay Horace, we will get you looked after” then Nero turned to all of the eight “We will get you all looked after, you are safe here my friend” he said ensuring all of the Messengers heard him. He studied the small group, seeing still more faces in shock, clothing tattered and scars or fresh wounds adorned their faces and heads. These men have been through hell he thought turning to see the small group of people gathering to find out who had come to their little safe haven.

Nero spotted Gilread and Meric, nodding for the two to approach he leaned into his right hand and friend “Can you ensure the soldiers get setup, we need to find them shelter and food” and Gildread nodded motioning for Meric to follow.

He looked over to see Vira already motioning for the Emisarries to follow her as she nodded to Nero, knowing he would want to deal with the Messengers himself. He led the eight towards his small tent, showing them in as others brought chairs from their own tents or found within the main hall, he thanked each person as they left, the Messengers sitting in a small semi-circle facing Nero.

Standing there he regarded the group as they stared back “How did you all come to find the soldiers Horace?” he asked quietly speaking to the Messenger he knew, had known for many years in fact but the man in front of him was very different then the happy carefree man of aurtus he had known. He looked beaten and more reserved then the last time Nero had seen the Master Historian for the order. Messenger Horace McCourt had never had a keep, never administered a traditional flock, instead his mission in life had been to learn and record the history of the order and he did it with an enthusiasm Nero rarely saw in people. The Messenger looked around and then bringing his attention back to Nero began to speak.

“I was visiting the Keep in the town of silvers knoll when the soldiers moved in, myself and Messenger Postric were ushered to meet the new Lord Seer” he began closing his eyes as he tried to control his emotions “The new Seer strangled Messenger Lostrine with is mind Nero, for speaking against the injustice that was being propagated against his people, I” he paused taking a breath, Horace didn’t make eye contact instead chose to look at the floor as he continued, Nero could see the tears falling from his once jolly cheeks “I didn’t protest, I didn’t defend him, I just stood there in terror Nero, I let him die right in front of me” he finally stammered and Nero moved to his friend, putting a hand on his shoulder and squeezing it reassuringly “It wouldn’t have mattered my friend, had you spoken out, he would have killed you too” he said gently, urging the man to go on.

“He kept me around, like a trophy as I watched the people of the village turned into nothing more then slaves, some killed as an example, others put to work, growing food or mining, the results of that labor sent by carts to the capital” he said finally looking up and making eye contact with Nero, oh those haunted eyes he thought lamenting the once carefree person he had been, but Nero had a feeling he would never truly be again “After months of watching the horrors and injustice I was able to sneak out of my room in the keep, helped by Messenger Jioro here” he said motioning to a tall thin quiet man who simply nodded, his face a mask of utter seriousness as he stood there “We made it out of the village, moving north, not knowing where else to go, I had heard east was covered as the Empress’s troops had begun to setup for an invasion of the East, finally we met up with the others, they too were going North, there were originally twenty of us, but the demons found us, those screamers and tore apart ten of us, the other two died along the way from injuries” he finished and now Horace was open faced crying and Nero threw his arms around the man in a caring embrace “You couldn’t have done anything my friend, you have made it and now you can begin to help heal the land” he whispered.

His friend looked up his face a mask of confusion “What do you mean Nero, the Empress has enslaved her people, she put mages in power to rule over them, what can we possibly do?” his friend pleaded and Nero stepped back, brandishing the ring and showing it to the other Messengers. “With the emissaries here, I will ask to enact the agreement in Vicor” he stated and heard the gasp from the small group. He knew what they were thinking, not in two hundred years, since the Accord had been agreed to have the Agreement been enforced. To do that, to allow that would be to set a dangerous precedent and everyone knew it.

It would require the Emissaries to concur and then it would require them to summon enough troops to enforce it, they all knew this. “What is the agreement?” came a voice from the door and Nero turned to see Gilread walking in, looking at the faces of the other Messengers and mirroring their concern. Nero smiled at his friend and motioning him to join them. Horace cleared his throat and looked to Nero, who nodded giving him permission to tell one who was not of the cloth about the concords of Aurtus.

“Well, two hundred and fifty years ago, in the country of kilren, a country that now no longer exists, the Emperor passed on without an heir, the country imploded, noble against noble as they tried to seize power, it was so bloody and devastating to not only the country itself but also to its neighbors nearly pulling the entire continent into a war that the eight rulers of the land called a summit, the church was brought in and an agreement was struck” he began and Gilread looked on with interest, the name of the country meaning nothing to him as it ceased to exist well before his fathers father roamed the earth.

Horace collected his thoughts and then continued taking on the air of a professor giving a lecture, Nero masked the smile it was good to see some of his old friend despite all that happened he thought. “All Eight Monarchs and Eight Lord Regents at the time agreed that if a ruler died and a direct heir could not be found then the church could step in acting as caretaker of the country until such time as the nobles unanimously voted in a new king, during the agreement, no country could invade or otherwise take advantage of the country in question” he stated. Gilread looked confused “But we have a Empress, how could the agreement be enacted?” he aske simply and Nero looked to Horace who shot an uncomfortable look at the Lord Regent and with a sigh he continued “Because the Emperor has died, without an heir the Lord Regent can declare his marriage null and void, thus removing the Empress’s claim to the throne and allowing the Church to take stewardship of the land” he finished not making eye contact with Gilread.

Horace understood they were treading in murky waters and to do this would set a dangerous precedent, one that could irrevocably damage relations between the rulers and the church. “Horace, these are extreme circumstances, requiring the church to take extreme measures” he said gently knowing his friends’ thoughts.

His friend nodded and finally looked up at the Newly minted Lord Regent “I understand Nero, but this could be seen as a power play by the church” he said giving voice to the most obvious fear the Rulers of the various countries would have. Nero nodded “I understand, and we will need to tread carefully, not to be seen as taking advantage but instead saving the country” he finished knowing they needed to do this and knowing that if they didn’t the country was doomed. Food was brought in and the group ate mostly in silence and Nero ate with them, enjoying the company of his fellow Messengers for the first time in a long time he thought. Gilread stayed as well talking with some of the Messengers, taking their mind off the perilous journey and horrors they had been exposed to.

At the end of the meal Nero said his goodbyes and departed for the main hall. He had to convince Lusor and Dever’s emissaries to stand behind him in this decision, for without them the plan would be stillborn. Entering the large hall, he noticed the workers had left, allowing the Emissaries some time to eat and rest, they now sat in the large room where a table and chairs had been brought in for them. Nero nodded approvingly when he noticed Vira by the entrance. “Thank you Vira, can you ensure we are not disturbed” he said, and the woman nodded, smiling at Nero she didn’t know his plans, but the hope on his face was enough for her, for the moment.

“Good Evening Emissaries, sorry to keep you waiting, I wanted to ensure our brothers ate and were comfortable before we met” Nero said getting approving nods from both of the men. “How are they Loprin asked his concern evident Nero smiled “They will recover, though it might take a while” he stated and Hutchin shook his head “So many horrors in this place Nero, the land will not heal quickly” he simply said and all three men let the statement hang in the air as each reflected on it, knowing how true the statement was.

Hutchin broke the silence as he regarded Nero “So Lord Regent Nero, you have asked for assistance, our Lords have seen fit to send us, there emissaries, they take what is going on here seriously and as cause for severe concern, how what is it you require to save our brethren, our church and this country?” he asked all three taking seats around the small table as the two Emissaries regarded Nero with cautious expressions.

Nero returned the gaze, organizing his thoughts, this was a critical moment he knew. He was a new Lord Regent, not one who was voted in but one who merely happened to be there to take the ring, though they hadn’t asked he was sure they suspected. The knight council was dead, meaning that he was the only leader the church had in Vicor and anything he asked for would be suspect since there was no consensus, the order of knights, the council that advised the Lord Regent was seen as a check to the Lord Regents power and one that was crucial to the leadership of the church.

Whatever he asked for would be scrutinized closely he he thought looking at the cautious look of these two men. Finally he took a breath and began “I know what I am about to say might seem extreme, but please hear me out” he began, the two men nodding, there look not changing as they waited for Nero to speak. Taking a breath the Lord Regeant leaned forward and began to speak, the words coming from the horror and pain he had witnessed, from the death of the Lord Regent to the slaughter of so many innocents, the domination of the mages must end he thought, but that was for another time, first he had to save his country, his people, his Messengers.

“The country has been seized, it has been subjugated the people turned into slaves and slaughtered for the power and amusement of those in power. This was not the will of the Emperor rest his soul he was a good ruler, a just ruler. Was he here now, he would have his wife removed? It is that I ask the Emissaries, I ask the other Lord Regents to band with me, to agree with me and enact the Agreement, I will state the marriage of the Emperor to this woman, this Victoria was not consummated and is in fact null, this will remove her right to rule and allow the church to step in, to fulfill its part of the agreement. We will then be able to set the country right again” Nero said, holding his breath as he looked at the two Emissaries, their faces blank of expression neither one betraying his thoughts on his words.

The room was silent for a long time as all three regarded each other the two men searching Nero’s face as if looking for something. Finally, Loprin spoke. “This is a serious action you ask us to take Nero, this is an action that will have repercussions throughout the land, not just in Vicor, this is not something we can agree to easily.” He began and Nero leaned forward to speak again and Loprin held up his hand “I am not saying there isn’t cause or precedent to interceded, it is just there are political consequences that stretch far outside this one country, we will need time to discuss this ourselves” he finished looking to Hutchin who nodded, again his face devoid of emotion. Nero looked between the two for a moment not understand and then it dawned on him, they didn’t want him here, they needed to talk, and he smiled nervously. “Of course, I will leave someone outside, should you need anything, merely ask” he said getting up and slightly bowing to the two men.

Nero slowly walked towards the door, every step second guessing, doubting, wondering if he had conveyed how serious his request was, how bad things were in the country, if only he could have given more examples he thought kicking himself for not laying out the Empress’s sins before asking for such an extreme solution. But it was now in the hands of these two men, if they denied his request, Vicor was lost and the only thing Nero would be able to do was be a Lord Regent in exile. He walked out of the building to find Meric and Gilread waiting on him. Both men smiling as he closed the door behind him, his shoulders slumping in worry and defeat. “Was it that bad?” Meric asked gently looking worried at Nero. The Messenger smiled weakly “I am no politician, nor am I a wordsmith, I am a humble Messenger, I fear my ability to convey how desperate our need is, is well beyond my ability” he said and Gilread shook his head

“They have crossed the land, they have seen what the Empress has done, they will agree” he said, and Nero looked up at his friend. He was so sure, not just saying it to make Nero feel better he thought, but sure they would agree with him. Gilread had such faith in him and he smiled “Thank you my friend, I am going to sit for a while and reflect, if they summon me, please let me know” he said, the two men nodding as Nero walked past, heading for a small tent that was used for storage, with his tent being used by the Messengers this was the only place he knew he could be alone.

Nero sat alone among the boxes as the light outside began to wane and nighttime descended upon the complex. He didn’t light a lamp, but merely sat there in the dark, praying for wisdom and patience. The former he needed, the latter he wanted but neither came as time went by slowly and he waited to find out the fate of his people, his country and himself. At some point Nero dozed off, the dark quiet room lulling him as his worry acted like a lullaby. He wasn’t sure how long he slept for and rested quietly until a gentle hand shook his shoulder “You are needed” came Gilread’s voice as he whispered in the dark. Nero came awake at once, looking around the room and noticing that only a small light peaked in from outside, Gilread having left the lamp in the doorway, enough for him to see, but not bright enough to disturb Nero.

The Lord Regent smiled up at his friend. “Did they say anything?” he asked hopefully and Gilread shook his head. “Only that you were needed” and Nero nodded, stretching and rising from the chair. Nero walked to the door with the two men in tow and crossed the open courtyard, his thoughts reeling as doubt plagued his mind. How long had they deliberated he wondered, was it too long or not long enough he tried to think, but he had little experience in this area as he tried to keep a calm exterior as he approached the large hall.

It was still dark outside, and the camp was quiet, Nero had no idea how late or early it was and didn’t trust himself to ask is friends. He entered the hall Both Meric and Gilread staying outside as the Lord Regent continued in alone. The room was dimly lit, the moon bringing light in through the still partially open ceiling as he made his way across the expansive stone floor. At the table the two Emissaries turned to regard the Lord Regeant, giving him the feeling of a school child sent to see the principal. “Emissaries” Nero said breathing slowly as not to show his panic and bowed as the two men sat cooly across the table. “Lord Regent Nero, please sit” Emissary Loprin announced, motion to the chair in front of Nero. He sat and regarded the two men, willing himself not to fidget, he would not show these men how nervous he was Nero vowed, eyeing the two men as they continued to sit there stalwart and silent. It seemed as if an eternity passed between the three of them before Emissary Hutchin finally spoke. The smaller man leaning forward his blue eyes continuing to regard Nero. Niether of the men giving away any clue as to what they had decided.

“Lord Regent Nero, we have discussed your recommendation” he began Nero held his breath mentally saying a short prayer “After careful consideration of all the facts, we approve, in the morning we will send messages to our perspective Lord Regents requesting troops, we will rendezvous with them and march on the capital, there we will take it by force removing the Empress and installing yourself as caretaker of the realm, however because of the seriousness of this situation we will also be bringing our own knights council made up of members of the Chuch from Lusor and Dever, this will be a temporary measure until we can refill the ranks of your own knights council, do you understand” Hutchin said and Nero could not believe his ears, for a moment he sat stunned looking between the two men as if at any moment they would burst out laughing, the whole thing being a joke. Nero realized he had not spoken as the two men began to look to each other as if the silence might be getting uncomfortable “I understand and agree” he finally stated, not knowing what else to say. The two men nodded, standing as they did so “Tomorrow will be a big day Lord Regent, and the coming week will be even more eventful, I suggest we get some rest and reconvene once we hear back from the Church” Emissary Loprin stated.

The three left the building, Vira there motioned for the two Emissaries to follow her and locked eyes with Nero as she did. He nodded smiling at her and he could see the relief, she was not privy to the specifics, but Nero’s face told her there was hope and that was all she needed. Standing there on the steps of the building he looked up towards the moon and said a silent prayer of thanks, his prayers had finally been answered.

Someone cleared his throat closeby and Nero looked to see Messenger McCourt standing there looking around nervously “Horace, whats wrong?” he asked smiling at his friend “It’s a good day my friend, a good day indeed” Nero told him and he could see Horace relax a little. “I take it the Church will assist in taking back Vicor, I thought they might” he said and the Lord Regent, finally beginning to feel his role nodded. “We will know the specifics later in the week, but they did agree” he said smiling at his friend.

Horace’s smile faltered “You know she has mages, that she is using their power to reinforce her rule” he said the question more of a statement. Nero’s smile also faltered “I know” he answered bitterly, and Horace looked uncomfortable for a moment. Juric, I can help, I know how to ensure we can combat her mages, we can overcome her power” he said fiercely and Nero stepped down bringing himself to his friends’ level.

“What do you know my friend?” he asked Horace smiled “The Church has done battle with the mages before, you know this, what you don’t know is that the weapons and armor used in war is stored in an armory, one that was known only to a few including the old historian who cataloged it all” he answered triumphantly and Nero’s eyes widened. Everyone knew the church had gone to war with the mages, helping to bring the devastating Mage War to an end. This was known to every messenger, but was it possible that the weapons, the long-lost runic armor that protected those soldiers from the power those mage’s yielded could still exist. “Where?” he simply asked and Horace smiled pulling a map from beneath his robes.

“The mages need to be stopped Nero, once and for all, they have gone too far this time” his friend said the hate and anger flowing off the words and his friend nodded they had he thought finally gone too far, the church had been forgiving before, that had been a mistake and he nodded “There will be an accounting my friend” he simply said and Horace handed the map to Nero.

Turning he called over his shoulder “I will be by your side, I will help with whatever you need Lord Regent” he said calling him by his official title for the first time and Nero smiled, he liked the sound of it he thought putting the map into his own robes.

Nero walked back to his small tent, it felt as if a heavy weight had been finally lifted as things were finally turning, finally heading for a resolution and he would spearhead that change, he would be able to finally protect his people he thought as he found Gilread and Meric still up and waiting for him.

“We did it” he said and both men clapped him on the back quietly cheering as they stood there basking in the good news. “That’s great Nero, finally things can begin to turn around” Meric said hugging Gilread. He watched the two men smiling, enjoying watching the unabashed show of love, something that had been lacking in this new world of the Empress’s New Order.

“Lord Regent Nero, may I speak to you” came an unfamiliar voice and Nero turned to find Messenger Jioro, he looked better having cleaned up after his long journey, Jioro was the one who helped Horace escape, regarding the man he looked angry and nervous. Nero stepped down “Whats wrong my friend” he said about to take a step towards him and then in a flash his face twisted with anger as a dagger flashed from beneath his robes, as he thrust it Nero watching the blade come at him a blur crossed in front of him and in a moment he watched in horror as the knife meant for him plunged into the chest of his friend Gilread fell to the ground gasping, Jioro looking shocked and then he turned his head up the anger back as a malevolent grin spread across his face “The Empress will overcome your pitiful attempt to bring her down, she will create her glorious new order the mundanes will serve her or die, the mages will finally take there rightful place as lords of this world” and then Jioro bit into something his face wincing as foam escaped from his mouth just as soldiers came around the corner running and shouting at the small group. Jioro fell, a soldier quickly went to one knee and then looking up at Nero shook his head, the would-be assassin was dead.

Nero then heard the gasp and looked down as Gilread lay there, a pool of blood spreading out below him and in an instant he was there and so was Meric, his lover and partner reaching down and cradling his body as he gently stroked Gilreads cheek “you’re going to be fine” he said through tears and Gilread tried to smile, a line of blood escaping down his cheek “Your such a liar” he said smiling. Gilreads eyes swiveled to look at Nero “Messenger, will you Marry us, I can’t leave this world without knowing I will see my love in the next” he wheezed as more blood rolled from his lips. It was said that those who Married in this world would always be reunited in the next, Nero understood his request but the hurt he felt, the pain of his friend lying there dying was almost overwhelming. But with tears in his eyes he extended one shaking hand and gently brushed a lock of the raven colored hair off his forehead. “Today, I present Buris Gilread servant of Aurtus and Holin Meric beloved of Buris and ask you to attend witness to this union of souls to your kingdom, may there life force bond in this world to be reunited in the next, allow them happiness and prosperity” he started and then hesitated hitching and with a breath finally finished the incantation “For as long as they both shall live”. With the utterance of the final decree he placed shaking and unsure hands on the heads of the two men “It is my honor to present you to this world and the next, in with the witness and light of Aurtus as joined in the eyes of the gods for all eternity” he finished and watched as Gilread smiled, wincing as pain shot through his body as Meric still held him gently despite the blood still pooling around both of them “I.. I love” he began and then the light left his friends eyes. Meric through his head back and an anguished scream rang out across the sky as his love, his life, his husband left this world. Nero, tears freely pouring down his cheeks leaned over his friend and whispered the final blessing, commiting his soul to Aurtus. Gently putting his arms around both the men he sat there rocking them gently, crying as he continued to simply hold them.

In his mind the hate that had been growing finally spread throughout his soul the mages will page for this he thought, the fire of hate and worse, the flames of fanaticism engulfed his soul as his mission was fully realized.
